answer: Behavioral correlation scoring tracks how account pairs share timing, wording, and transaction partners, building a trellis of verified interactions that grows denser over time. Scores above threshold flag likely shared operators, letting enforcement revoke reputations and flag the whole cluster, so an attacker must maintain a natural harbor of distinct behavior patterns per fake identity. Each identity also needs its own payment rails and IP thread to avoid linkage, raising marginal cost per Sybil well above the value a single identity can extract.
